transcript.content: Hello, welcome. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm here because of some issues at work. I teach preschool, and... well, it's just that the second I spot balloons at school, even if they're all the way across the hallway... my chest gets really tight. I just sort of freeze up for a moment before I can think clearly about what I’m supposed to be doing. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Do you ever feel anxious or have similar reactions even when you're just thinking about balloons being present at school, like before you actually see them?
Um... no, not really. I don't... I don't really think about them unless they're actually there. It's mostly just when I see them.
Are there certain types of balloons or situations involving balloons that bother you more than others, or is it any balloon regardless of size, color, or how they’re being used?
Um... no, I haven't really noticed a difference. It's just... any of them, I guess. I don't really look at them long enough to care about the color or... or how big they are. Just any balloon.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain areas or activities at school specifically because you might encounter balloons?

Um... yeah, I guess so. Lately, I've been... asking my aides to handle the birthday circles. Or if there's a festival table or something with them nearby, I just move away. 

If I absolutely have to stay... I just keep my distance. I just focus on getting through it and... try not to look at them.
When you feel that tightness in your chest around balloons, does it ever feel like it comes on suddenly and peaks within minutes? Or does it build up slowly and stay with you for a while?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't... I haven't really thought about it like that. It just... happens when they're around. I don't really know if it peaks or anything, it's just... uncomfortable.
When you see balloons, do you ever feel like your heart starts racing or you suddenly feel like you can’t breathe, like you’re having a panic attack?
Um... no, not really. I don't think so. My heart doesn't race or anything like that. I just... I just don't like being near them. It's not a panic attack.
Do you ever find yourself feeling anxious or worrying about balloons when you're not actually around them, like when you're at home or thinking about going to school?
Um... no. Not really. I don't... I don't really think about them when I'm at home. It's just... when they're actually there.
Have you ever had to cancel or avoid doing something outside of school, like going to a party or a store, because you were worried you might see balloons there?
Um... no. I don't think I've ever done that. I still go to the store and... things like that. I don't really cancel plans.
Has this reaction to balloons ever caused you any problems in your personal life, like trouble with relationships, sleep, or other activities you used to enjoy?

Um... well, it's mostly just work. I teach kindergarten, so... they come up. I've had to ask the aides to take over when there's a birthday or a celebration. And... I guess I missed helping with an art table at a festival recently that I was supposed to run. My supervisor asked about it. But... it's just work stuff, really.
Is your discomfort limited only to balloons, or do you feel similarly uncomfortable in other situations where you might feel trapped or unable to escape easily, even if balloons aren't present?
No, it's... just the balloons. I don't really have a problem with feeling trapped or anything like that. Just... when they're around.
Have you ever found yourself feeling anxious or worried about balloons even when you weren't actually around them, like when you're at home or thinking about school?
Um... no. Not really. I don't really think about them when I'm at home. It's just... when I actually see them.

Outside of asking aides for help and stepping away from certain activities, has this fear of balloons ever led to any other consequences at work, like disciplinary action, reduced responsibilities, or conflicts with coworkers or supervisors?
Um... no. Not really. Just... what I mentioned before. My supervisor asked about the festival, but... that's it. No disciplinary action or anything like that.
Do you ever feel significant distress or have trouble functioning normally at work because of your reaction to balloons, like feeling overwhelmed or unable to focus on your job?

Um... yeah, a little. I mean... I have to ask the aides to handle the classroom celebrations now. And... I couldn't help with the art table at the festival, even though I planned it. My supervisor did ask about that... so I guess it's getting in the way of my normal duties.
When you see balloons at school, does the feeling of tightness in your chest happen right away, almost automatically, or does it take some time to build up?
Um... yeah, it's right away. The second I spot them, even if they're just across the hallway... my chest tightens up. I just kind of freeze for a moment before I can think clearly.

Even though you said you don’t think about balloons when you're not at school, have you ever felt anxious or worried about seeing them again when you're away, like when you're at home or planning for the next day?
Um... no. Not really. When I'm not there, I don't really think about it. I just... go home. I don't worry about it until I'm actually there and see them.
When you see balloons, does your chest tightening feel like an immediate physical reaction, or does it come more as a feeling of anxiety first?

Um... like I said a minute ago... it's just physical. Right away. The second I spot them, my chest tightens. I just... freeze. It happens before I can even think clearly about what I'm supposed to be doing.
